scope: f64 graph26 gg-to-HHH reduction with identical PolynomialNumerator provider and frozen shared masters. Coefficient preparation and actual master computation excluded; ordinary callback, lookup, transport, staging, allocation and contraction costs included.
master_policy: Per-process captures under the same ordered-request/backend policy, then one frozen handle shared by original and Rust; all-mode physical oracle separately checks literally one frozen union for all selections.
callback_policy: The same PolynomialNumerator provider and equal sampled rows, but unequal requested expansion heads/depths. Original Ninja reduces swapped bubble depth while this Rust baseline requests full depth for both orientations. No equal callback arithmetic claim.

provider.coefficient_heads: Factored multi-output SymJIT O2, evaluated only in physical preparation
provider.reduction_callbacks: Same PolynomialNumerator<f64> and generic Symbolica batched interpreter for direct/Mu/T3/T2; callbacks are not JIT compiled
provider.execution_span_scope: Individual direct/Mu/T3/T2 provider ABI decoding, interpreted evaluation and output writing; calls/rows/ns reported separately

symbolica.selection_scope: Setup-only partial catalog; unused stages need not execute. Numerator, geometry and masters are independent.

limitations: Diagnostic only: unrelated host activity and unreserved SMT sibling prevent acceptance.
Each selection is paired with original Ninja; cross-selection confidence intervals are not directly paired. Mode order rotates by width to expose, not eliminate, temporal drift.
Bootstrap intervals describe observed paired blocks, not general hardware or phase-space uncertainty.
One physical n5 rank4 graph and three fixed-helicity changing phase-space points; this is not the full benchmark acceptance suite.
The broader native selection covers five kernel families. Geometry and remaining reduction/integration/accumulation stay interpreted.
Frozen master lookup/transport time remains included; actual master computation is zero. Separate release execution reports measure actual backend computation.
All reports retain the ordinary allocation costs; no warmed allocation-free claim.
No numerical accuracy/domain extension: the reciprocal guard exposes overflowing f64 failure.
The de0f190 and 553f406 schedules were collected separately, not as paired before/after blocks. No causal speedup or paired before/after confidence interval is claimed.
No comparison with the older dba methodology; previous immutable archives are retained separately.

policy.below_20ms: retain and flag; never silently omit

prepared_schedule.completion: All 18 commands exited successfully; the coordinated build/numerical hold was released before archival and statistics validation.

runtime_change_scope: Within-call denominator reuse between quotient and correction stages; no persistent numerical-result cache. Rank specialization, native geometry and blocking experiments are excluded. Dependency revisions, provider/master policy and benchmark runtime API are unchanged.
comparison_scope: Every Rust selection is paired with original Ninja within its process. The separately collected de0f190 and 553f406 schedules are not directly paired before/after measurements; no causal speedup or paired before/after interval is inferred.
